feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
entry.summary: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.

entry.title: The Fed raises interest rates. And, EU proposes Canada become an 'associate member'
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time in years. And, the European Union has proposed that Canada become its first-ever "associate member."

entry.title: Pressure on global chokepoints drives Asia's increased use of Arctic Trade Routes
entry.summary: Asian nations began pilot voyages over a decade ago to find routes to Europe and the Middle East that were faster and less vulnerable to chokepoints. The ongoing war has added impetus to those efforts.

entry.title: Big questions - and key logistical details - loom ahead of China-U.S. summit
entry.summary: Despite the lingering questions, China remains optimistic about the summit.

entry.title: Rising gas prices fuel protests in countries around the world
entry.summary: Protests over rising fuel protest are happening around the world, a ripple effect as the Us war on Iran is dragging Saudi Arabia in deeper

entry.title: How the fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is affecting gas prices
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with oil markets expert Ellen R. Wald of the Atlantic Council about how the escalation in fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is affecting global oil and gas prices.

entry.title: With invite to join EU bloc, Canada's prime minister speaks to European Parliament
entry.summary: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks to the European Parliament, following the European Union's invitation to Canada to become an "associate member" of the bloc.

entry.title: EU offers Canada 'associate member' role; Trump calls it 'laughable'
entry.summary: The European Union backs Canada's bid to become the bloc's first "associate member," as Brussels seeks closer ties with Ottawa and Trump calls the idea "laughable."

entry.title: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
entry.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

entry.title: Russia seizes Ukrainian POWs, then it demands favors from their relatives
entry.summary: Russia is believed to be holding thousands of Ukrainian POWs. Russia is also tormenting the families of these prisoners by contacting their relatives on social media and demanding they help Russia.
